nativeEnforcementAvailable: The pinned app-server accepts turn/start params.sandboxPolicy of type workspaceWrite with a writableRoots array. Writes outside the task workspace plus the listed roots are denied natively before they land; fileChange items declined by that policy report status declined.
hostEnforcementImplemented: Task creation binds extraWriteDirs (canonicalized absolute paths, must exist) and denyPaths (workspace-relative prefixes, no .. or absolute roots) into the durable task record.
turn/start carries sandboxPolicy {type:workspaceWrite,writableRoots:[workspace,...extraWriteDirs]} whenever extraWriteDirs is bound, so extra roots are enforced by the native sandbox itself.

Every fileChange item reports its touched paths; each path is checked against workspace+extraWriteDirs+denyPaths and a durable write.scope.violation fact (kind OUT_OF_SCOPE or DENIED_PATH) is emitted per (path,kind) once.

Native rejections surface as facts: a declined fileChange/commandExecution item records NATIVE_FILE_REJECTED/NATIVE_EXEC_REJECTED; a failed commandExecution whose output mentions sandbox/denied/permission/outside-the-workspace records NATIVE_SANDBOX_REJECTED.
At each turn boundary a git diff --name-only + untracked-files sweep of the workspace verifies every touched name against denyPaths and emits DENIED_PATH violations for matches.
gap: denyPaths inside the workspace are not preemptively enforced: writableRoots grants the whole workspace to the native sandbox, so a model or command can write under a denied prefix during the turn and the violation is only detected at item completion or the turn boundary. The fact is honest and durable but the write already landed.

commandExecution items do not enumerate the paths a process wrote; out-of-scope writes through shell commands are caught only by the native writableRoots sandbox (outside workspace+extra roots) or by the turn-end git sweep (deny paths inside the workspace). A command that writes into a deny path and deletes its own tracks before the sweep would evade detection.
Violations are recorded, not rolled back: no content restore, file removal, or turn rewind is attempted on a detected violation.
currentBehavior: writeScope defaults to the task workspace. extraWriteDirs extend the native writableRoots policy; denyPaths are host-observed at item completion and at the turn seal. Every check writes a durable write.scope.violation event and a bounded writeScopeViolations projection on the task. enforcement reports APP_SERVER_WRITABLE_ROOTS+HOST_OBSERVED_DENYLIST; nothing is claimed as a preemptive deny-path gate.
scope: Verification is limited to paths the engine reports on fileChange items plus the workspace-visible git diff at a real boundary. Remote tool/service writes outside the local filesystem are not in scope.
